svg.title: Studge Pass relay trust boundary
svg.desc: Your devices hold the master password, the Secret Key and every unwrapped key. They sign operations and pin vault heads. The relay is untrusted: it stores ciphertext, wrapped keys and metadata, and can withhold or reorder data, which clients detect. The line between them carries only ciphertext, signatures and authentication messages.
svg.text: Relay trust boundary
The relay is treated as an attacker. Correctness never depends on it being honest.
Your devices — trusted
Master password + Secret Key
→ MUK → AK → VK → IK (memory only)
Signs every op and every head
Ed25519 device keys, certified by the account identity
Pins the last verified vault head
detects rollback, fork and missing history
Decrypts and authenticates locally
any tag or AAD mismatch is a hard error
Also on this side: the printed recovery kit and the guardians.
Nothing here is ever sent to the relay.
Relay — untrusted
Stores only: account_salt, wrapped AK,
wrapped vault/item keys, op ciphertext, heads
Sees metadata: ids, sizes, counts, timing, IP
cannot avoid it; see R-0101
Can withhold, delay, or refuse service
detected as a missing parent or a stalled head
Cannot read, forge, swap, reorder undetectably,
roll back a client that has a pinned head
OPAQUE means even a full database dump cannot be
used to guess passwords without the Secret Key.
HTTPS
requests
responses
only ciphertext,
signatures and
OPAQUE messages
cross the line
What never crosses the boundary
master password · password-equivalent hash · Secret Key · MUK · auth secret · AK · vault keys · item keys · plaintext item data · plaintext URLs
AGENTS.md rule 8 makes this a defect, not a trade-off, if any code path ever sends one of them.
